title: Theme Check flags "wordpress" identifier as REQUIRED — false positive, do not "fix" by renaming
body:
**Context:** WordPress.org's automated Theme Check scan on the release build reported:

```
REQUIRED: Found incorrect spelling or capitalization of WordPress in the file

Line 273:    'wordpress'      => [
Line 274:        'value' => 'wordpress',

```
**Why this is a false positive, not a bug:**

```
'wordpress' => [
    'value' => 'wordpress',
    'label' => 'WordPress',   // ← already correctly capitalized
],
```

The display text is already correct. The key/value are internal, code-level identifiers (used consistently the same way for every other social network), almost certainly feeding into things like a CSS/icon class or a stored customizer setting.

**Why we should not "fix" this by renaming the key/value:**

- Breaks consistency with every other entry in the array
- Risks breaking icon rendering, if value feeds a fa-{value} class construction
- Risks breaking backward compatibility for any site that already saved 'wordpress' as a selected value in its database

Theme Check's scanner does a blind text search for "wordpress" and doesn't understand code context — this is a well-known false-positive pattern for icon/data lookup tables. Renaming a working, consistently-used identifier just to silence a linter that's wrong here would trade real functionality/compatibility risk for a cosmetic pass on an automated check.

**Recommended resolution:** Leave the code as-is. The REQUIRED flag routes the release to WP.org's manual review queue rather than blocking it outright — a human reviewer will see the label is already correctly capitalized and can clear it. Document this decision here so it isn't "fixed" incorrectly in a future pass without this context.

title: Blocklisted file-extension patterns are unanchored, so ordinary filenames fail the check
body:
## Description

`Check_File_Check` matches its blocklist with `preg_grep` and no anchors, so a pattern intended to match a file *extension* matches that string anywhere in the path.

```php
// checks/class-file-check.php
$blocklist = array(
    …
    '\.dat' => __( 'Customizer import file', 'theme-check' ),
    '\.xml' => __( 'XML file', 'theme-check' ),
    '\.sh'  => __( 'Shell script file', 'theme-check' ),
    …
);

foreach ( $blocklist as $file => $reason ) {
    if ( $filename = preg_grep( '/' . $file . '/', $filenames ) ) {
```

`'\.sh'` is the worst of these because `sh` begins many ordinary words. Any CSS or JS file whose name contains `.sh…` is reported as a shell script and raises a **REQUIRED** error, which fails the automated scan on upload.

## Step-by-step reproduction instructions

1. Add a stylesheet named `assets/styles/tokens.sys.shape.css` to any theme.
2. Run Theme Check.

**Expected:** no error; it is a CSS file.

**Actual:**

> REQUIRED: `tokens.sys.shape.css` Shell script file found. This file must not be in the production version of the theme.

## Scope

Four patterns produce false positives on plausible filenames:

| File | Reported as |
| --- | --- |
| `assets/styles/tokens.sys.shape.css` | Shell script file |
| `assets/styles/tokens.sys.sheet.css` | Shell script file |
| `assets/js/theme.shortcodes.js` | Shell script file |
| `assets/styles/layout.shadow.css` | Shell script file |
| `assets/data.database.json` | Customizer import file |
| `assets/db.sqlite3` | SQL dump file |

`.shape`, `.sheet`, `.shortcodes`, `.shadow`, `.database`, and `.sqlite3` are all normal names. `shape` in particular is the name of one of Material Design's token axes, so `tokens.sys.shape.css` is a natural filename for any theme following that system.

## Suggested fix

Anchor the extension patterns at the end of the string:

```php
if ( $filename = preg_grep( '/' . $file . '$/', $filenames ) ) {
```

That suits every entry that is an extension. Three entries are not extensions and would need care: `'^.+[a-zA-Z0-9]'` (hidden files, already anchored at the start), `'error_log'`, and `'__MACOSX'`. Splitting the blocklist into “extension” and “exact name” groups, each matched with its own anchoring, would be clearer than one array with mixed semantics.

## Environment info

- Theme Check 20260901
- WordPress 7.1
- PHP 8.3

title: Fix: Clear theme cache after adding extra_theme_headers
body:
## What?
<!-- Link this PR to its associated issue with an appropriate keyword: Closes, See, Follow up to, etc. -->
Closes #494 

<!-- In a few words, what is the PR actually doing? -->
This PR ensures that the "License" and "License URI" fields are correctly displayed in the Theme Info summary box when checking the currently active theme.

## Why?
<!-- Why is this PR necessary? What problem is it solving? Reference any existing previous issue(s) or PR(s), but please add a short summary here, too -->
When Theme Check is run against the currently active theme, the "License" and "License URI" fields are missing from the visual summary box at the top of the WP Admin page. This occurs because WordPress caches the active theme's `WP_Theme` object early during initialization, long before Theme Check hooks into the `extra_theme_headers` filter to register these license fields.

## How?
<!-- How is your PR addressing the issue at hand? What are the implementation details? -->
This PR:
1. Adds a call to `wp_clean_themes_cache( false );` immediately after registering the `extra_theme_headers` filter in `theme-check.php`.
2. This busts the WordPress theme cache and forces `wp_get_theme()` to re-parse the active theme, successfully capturing the new headers.

## Testing Instructions
<!-- Please include step by step instructions on how to test this PR. -->
1. Activate a theme on your site that has `License:` and `License URI:` defined in its `style.css`
2. Navigate to **Appearance > Theme Check**.
3. Select the currently active theme from the dropdown and click **Check it!**.
4. Look at the **Theme Info** summary box at the top of the results page.
5. Verify that both the `License` and `License URI` fields are now correctly displayed in the summary box.

title: Automate release process with a GitHub action
body:
## What?
Automate the release process of the plugin with a GitHub action.

## Why?
To automate the process, lowering the effort of releasing new versions and avoiding the need to manually repeat tasks prone to errors.


## How?
By adding a GitHub action.

There will be a new action in the 'actions' section of the repo. The user will be able to select the type of release to launch (patch, minor, major) and a PR will be created with the new version. If everything is OK with the newly created PR and it is merged to `master` branch it will fire a release to the wordpress.org plugin directory.

## Demo
The code for this change was adapted from the Create Block Theme repo. Here is a screencast of the release process in that repo that this PR brings to Theme-check plugin.

[Screencast from 10-10-24 16:05:23.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fa36690-97de-46fd-924d-f2ce84af59dc)


## Blocked by
The Github action assumes that the plugin is using semantic versioning.
The implementation of this action is blocked by: https://github.com/WordPress/theme-check/issues/469

title: Check the number of h1 elements on block theme templates
body:
## What?
Check the number of h1 elements on each block theme template.
This check only runs when checking block themes.

**Results:**
- If one template has multiple `h1` tags, it outputs a REQUIRED change error.
- If a template has zero `h1` tags, it outputs a WARNING.
- If a template has only one `h1` tag, it outputs nothing.

## How
It iterates over each block of a template and looks for core/heading or core/post-title with level one to determine the number of h1 blocks that will be printed on a page.

## Why?
To help theme creators use one `h1` tag per template following accessibility recommendations like: https://www.a11yproject.com/posts/how-to-accessible-heading-structure/

body:
When running Theme Check against the currently active theme, the "License" and "License URI" fields are missing from the visual Theme Info summary box at the top of the page. This happens even when the headers are correctly defined in style.css.

Checking an inactive theme with the same headers works perfectly, and the License information is displayed.

This issue was first highlighted in Support Forums: https://wordpress.org/support/topic/license-and-license-uri-not-listed-in-theme-details/

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Activate a theme that has License: and License URI: defined in its style.css.
2. Navigate to Appearance > Theme Check.
3. Select the active theme from the dropdown and click "Check it!".
4. Look at the Theme Info summary block at the top of the results.

### Expected Behavior
The License and License URI fields should be displayed in the Theme Info summary.

### Actual Behavior 
The License and License URI fields are completely missing from the Theme Info summary.

## What?

The plugin releases are (apparently) named after its release date:

title: Handle checks and results as a structured array instead of an array of strings.
body: ## What? Currently, the errors produced by the check class are a list of strings containing HTML tags. This makes using these messages difficult for something that's not printing the results to an HTML page. Exampe: ```php "WARNING: screenshot.png is 704.2 KB in size. Large file sizes have a negative impact on website performance and loading time. Compress images before using them." ``` ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4996f09b-149d-415c-a798-48b9deb395e9) If we the plugin can handle the messages as a list of objects (PHP relational arrays) and format just before outputting them, it would be easier to handle that in different formats (Html page, console output, JSON). Example of 2 different outputs being implemented (console and json in the console): https://github.com/WordPress/theme-check/pull/458 ## Expected The plugin could handle the errors like this. In this way, each output handler could format it accordingly without parsing or removing HTML. ```php $checks = array ( array( 'type' => 'ERROR', 'message' => 'This is an error text' ), array( 'type' => 'WARNING', 'message' => 'This is an warning error text' ), array( 'type' => 'INFO', 'message' => 'This is an info text' ), ) ```

title: Warn about jQuery usage on the front end
body:
While it has been widely known that [you might not need jQuery](https://youmightnotneedjquery.com/) for most of your interactive theme features, jQuery is still a common JavaScript dependency found in WordPress themes - for example, 7 out of the 11 default themes since Twenty Ten use jQuery in the frontend. 

A recent analysis of [the performance impact of using jQuery in WordPress themes](https://make.wordpress.org/themes/2021/10/04/the-performance-impact-of-using-jquery-in-wordpress-themes/
) determined that **jQuery is the most common JavaScript-based performance problem in themes** and that **Removing jQuery may lead to 80% less JavaScript load**. According to the analysis, most themes can easily substitute (modern) vanilla JavaScript and remove their reliance on jQuery with only minor changes.

To help theme developers make better choices in the future, I would like to add a warning to the theme-check plugin when themes enqueue 'jquery' on the front end (eg. `wp_enqueue_script`). The warning could reference the analysis and perhaps offer a link to an [article explaining how to switch to vanilla JavaScript](https://tobiasahlin.com/blog/move-from-jquery-to-vanilla-javascript/). 

If this idea seems reasonable, I am happy to work on a PR to add this.

title: Adapt checks for Full-Site Editing themes
body:
Full-site editing themes do not use mosts of the existing PHP template tags, CSS classes, or theme supports. They therefore currently do not pass the Theme Checker.

We should implement a way to modify the existing checks when an FSE theme is uploaded. These include:

- Required:
   - Tag display.
   - CSS classes
   - Avatar display
   - Hardcoded titles
   - Post navigation
   - Comment reply script
   - All basic checks
- Recommended:
   - Widget support
   - Navigation menu support
   - Post thumbnails support
   - Custom header and custom background support
   - Editor styles support

At the same time we should ensure that FSE themes have at least an `index.html` template, and a theme config file.

title: Sanitize checks fail if semi-colons are in strings
body:
https://wordpress.org/support/topic/add_setting-check-can-fail-even-if-callback-specified

Example to trigger:

```
$wp_customize->add_setting('foofoo', array(
  'foo'=>'string containing ; here',
  'sanitize_callback'=>'bar'
) );
```

Workaround for now: move the string into a variable outside the function call:

```
$str = 'string containing ; here';
$wp_customize->add_setting('foofoo', array(
  'foo'=>$str,
  'sanitize_callback'=>'bar'
) );
```

Fix: Regex in customizer.php check needs to be more robust.

Provide a unique namespace for everything the Theme defines in the public namespace, including options, functions, global variables, constants, post meta, etc.

We can check if they are namespaced with the theme slug.

title: Improve child theme support
body:
I have been looking at the code for textdomain to check that the textdomain matches the theme slug.

While doing so I realized that the theme check is checking the contents of the parent theme also when checking a child theme.

My proposal would be
- Only include the parent files when running the plugin locally but not when uploading the child theme to w.org
- Not running some checks if it is a child theme like `style_needed.php` as the styles should already be included in the parent theme.

title: Theme Tag functionality [Info]
body:
"The theme tags in style.css and description must match the what the theme actually does in respect to functionality and design."

Add checks for 
- [ ] buddypress - I am not sure what the best check is here.
- [ ] featured-images `add_theme_support( 'post-thumbnails' );`
- [ ] custom-header `add_theme_support( 'custom-header' );`
- [ ] custom-background `add_theme_support( 'custom-background' );`
- [ ] custom-menu `register_nav_menus()`
- [ ] editor-style `add_editor_style()`
- [ ] flexible-header "Uses ‘flex-height’ and/or ‘flex-width’ parameter of `add_theme_support( 'custom-header' );`"
- [ ] post-formats `add_theme_support( 'post-formats' );`
- [ ] theme-options `add_action( 'customize_register' );`
- [ ] threaded-comments `wp_enqueue_script( 'comment-reply' );`

title: Use the Customizer for implementing theme options [Required]
body: Check for `add_settings_section`, `add_settings_field`, `register_setting`, `settings_fields` and `do_settings_sections`

title: Generic tokenizer checking
body:
The checks using regex ain't great. For some checks like the recent text domain checks, the tokenizer was used. This can be made more generalized, to allow the tokenizer data to be only made once and then given to several checks.

This is a general issue to track the idea of using the tokenizer in multiple checks, and having the actual token process in the main check system instead of in each check.
